subject: IP assertion + outbound audit bundle request for private deployment
messages:
From: Nadia Klein <nadia.k@veridianhealth.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment egress/IP inventory + auditor request

Ethan —

Thanks for the walkthrough today. Our auditors (internal compliance) have asked us to provide a consolidated list of outbound IPs and firewall expectations for the private (VPC) deployment of Redwood in our staging account. Specifically they want:

- Definitive source IP ranges (or ranges you require us to allow) for control-plane callbacks and telemetry.
- Recommended firewall rules (ports, SNI domains, and whether DNS to .redwood.ai must be allowed).
- Evidence that those IPs are stable (or rotation window) and that TLS and cert chains are enforced.
- A small bundle for our SOC/IT team showing logs / attestations you can provide (audit logs, KMS signoff, retention statements).

Can you provide an "egress audit bundle" we can drop into our audit folder? We need something we can hand to our auditor by EOD Wednesday (10/6). Also let us know whether we should NAT outbound traffic through our edge or whether Redwood will require any sticky source addresses.

Appreciate a quick confirmation of timeline.

—Nadia
Nadia Klein
Director, Cloud Security
Veridian Health

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Klein <nadia.k@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment egress/IP inventory + auditor request

Nadia —

Thanks — we can do this. High level answers & next steps below, then I list a couple quick clarifying Qs so we produce exactly what your auditors need.

Summary (short):
- We will assemble an "egress audit bundle" containing: authoritative outbound IP manifest, recommended firewall ruleset (ports, SNI domains), TLS cert chain notes, and a short evidence checklist explaining what Redwood can attest to (control plane callback IPs, retention windows for audit logs, KMS integration evidence).
- ETA: initial bundle by COB Tue 10/6 (per your ask).

Clarifying Qs:
1) Will your deployment NAT all egress through your customer-managed NAT (preferred), or are you planning to route some egress via a customer edge that we will see as non-deterministic? (If NAT'd on your side we provide the destination IPs you must allow.)
2) Do auditors require signed statements on company letterhead for any items (we can provide an attestation PDF from Redwood Security if needed)?

I'll put together the manifest now and loop in our security/ops folks (laura and marissa). Attaching preliminary stub: egress-ip-manifest-v1.csv (list of candidate destination ranges).

Regards,
Ethan Park
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment egress/IP inventory + auditor request

Ethan / Laura —

Thanks for the heads-up, copied Nadia in the prior thread. Operational plan (what we'll produce):

- Authoritative IP manifest (CSV + human readable): per-service destination ranges for control plane, telemetry, blobs, and model fetch (if applicable). We will flag which ranges are stable vs. rotating (rotation window and expected frequency).
- Firewall guidance (single-page): ports, TLS/SNI expectations, DNS allowances (we recommend allowing DNS to *.redwood.ai for cert validation; SNI enforcement is required for some proxies).
- Evidence checklist: list of artifacts we can include in the bundle (control-plane TLS cert chain, API audit log excerpt (redacted), KMS key metadata, SOC2 statement reference, and timestamps showing retention period).
- Attestation: short signed letter from Security on Redwood letterhead confirming the above for the specified account and environment.

Operational questions for you, Nadia:
- Please confirm the account id / VPC tag we should reference in the attestation (helps auditors tie docs to environment).
- Is there a specific format your auditor prefers (ZIP vs tar.gz vs single PDF)? We'll produce both the tar.gz bundle and a single consolidated PDF.

Attach: evidence-checklist.md (stub). I'll coordinate with Ben Carter (ops) for an audit log excerpt and signed cert chain.

Goal: bundle delivered by 2026-10-06 COB; if auditors need earlier, let us know and we'll prioritize the attestation PDF first.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Klein <nadia.k@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment egress/IP inventory + auditor request

Nadia —

Bundle attached: redwood-egress-audit-bundle-v1.tar.gz (contains manifest, firewall guidance PDF, cert chain, redacted audit log excerpt, and signed attestation). Highlights below for your SOC team: 

- Destination IPs (summary):
  * control-plane: 54.23.12.0/24 (stable)
  * telemetry/metrics endpoints: 54.23.13.0/24 (rotation window: monthly; see manifest)
  * model fetch CDN: 34.120.44.0/22 (CDN may rotate; we recommend allowing *.redwood-cdn.net SNI)

- Ports/Protocols: 443 (HTTPS) required. We recommend allowing outbound TCP/443 to the ranges above. TLS with SNI validation is enforced for all connections.

- DNS: allow DNS resolution for *.redwood.ai and *.redwood-cdn.net for certificate validation. If your NAT strips SNI, please use customer-managed NAT that preserves SNI or alternatively let us host a fixed egress IP for the control plane (requires contract appendix).

- Evidence summary included: KMS key metadata (redacted), audit log excerpt (last 72 hours, redacted UIDs), cert chain PEMs, signed attestation.pdf. Full list inside evidence-checklist.md in the bundle.

Next steps: please confirm the VPC tag/account id to include in the final attestation and tell us whether you will sign the DocuSign appendix (if you want Redwood to host fixed egress IPs). If auditors want a letter on Redwood letterhead only, we can provide that immediately.

Thanks — let me know if you'd like a short walkthrough of the bundle.

Best,
Ethan Park
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
